solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Credit claimed by bowler for sensational headline

indicators.note: something claimed by another is taken into it, so the credit abbreviation goes inside the bowler

parts.note: a seamer is a cricket bowler who makes the ball move off the seam

explanation.surface: A cricketer who has bowled well grabs the glory, and the papers splash his feat across the front page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests a hat; in cricket a SEAMER is a type of bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A screamer is slang for a banner headline in large, attention-grabbing type.

clue.text: Staff enlisting characters from the Far East

indicators.note: enlisting means taking in recruits, so the staff contains the characters

parts.note: a cane is a walking staff
tones are characters or qualities, as in the tone of a place

explanation.surface: Personnel are recruiting people from East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but means a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonese describes people, food or speech of Canton (Guangzhou) in southern China.

clue.text: In conclusion, newspaper upping ante finally — prepare for attack

indicators.note: in places the turned-up newspaper inside the word for conclusion

parts.note: the end is the conclusion

indicators.note: in a down clue, upping means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of ante

explanation.surface: A paper raising the stakes at last is told to brace itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upping ante' looks like raising a bet; 'upping' reverses RAG.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fencer's call warning an opponent to take a defensive stance before a bout.

clue.text: Scot's shot over a small republic

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a shot of Scotch whisky is a dram of malt

explanation.surface: A Scotsman fires over a little country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests firing; it is a measure of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the Mediterranean, small in area, which became a republic in 1974.

clue.text: Smooth heads seen in reflection, umpteen baldies

indicators.note: heads picks the opening letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Many bald men see their polished heads reflected in a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen in' is a link. 'Heads' looks like bald pates but picks first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub something is to polish or smooth it by friction.

clue.text: Request individual gets on your bike

parts.note: to beg is to request earnestly
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a person to be dismissed with a curt instruction to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets' is only a link. 'On your bike' is British slang for 'go away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive commands telling someone to clear off immediately.

clue.text: Rod, youthful server

parts.note: a bar is a metal rod
tender means young, as in tender years

explanation.surface: A young waiter named Rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name; it is a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks behind a bar, so a server in a pub.

clue.text: Enjoy oneself, or be sad

definitions.meaning: to party and dance with abandon
be low or depressed, feeling down

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to dance and let loose, and to feel depressed or gloomy.

clue.text: Language comprehended by Armenian or Serbian

indicators.note: comprehended means contained, so the language is held inside these words

explanation.surface: A tongue understood by speakers from two eastern European nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehended' suggests understanding; it means included.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse is the medieval Scandinavian tongue of the Vikings.

clue.text: Warm pieces turned over

indicators.note: turned over tells us the word for pieces is read backwards in this clue

parts.note: pieces is slang for guns, firearms

explanation.surface: Bits of something are flipped while they heat up.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug means comfortably cosy, sheltered and warm.

clue.text: A British politician joining party, US-style: reaction tested here?

parts.note: Labour is a British party, and the American spelling drops the U
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A British MP signs up to a party spelt the American way, and wonders how it will be received.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reaction' looks political but means a chemical reaction. 'Joining' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemical reactions are tried out by scientists in a lab, the place for experiments.

clue.text: See Portland and Augusta possibly consuming large mineral

parts.note: to tour a place is to see its sights

indicators.note: consuming means the state swallows the letter for large

parts.note: Portland and Augusta are both cities in the US state of Maine, which they exemplify
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A traveller visits two American cities that happen to contain a big deposit of some rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Portland and Augusta also suggest Oregon and Georgia, but together they point to MAINE, which has both.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourmaline is a crystalline boron silicate gemstone, a mineral found in many colours.

clue.text: Oddly, isn't entirely put in

indicators.note: oddly signals that the letters of the word isn't are arranged in an odd way

parts.note: all means entirely, completely

explanation.surface: Strangely, something is not quite complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' suggests odd letters but is the anagram signal for ISN'T, giving INST.
explanation.definitionFit: To install equipment or software is to fit or set it up in place.

clue.text: Frank thus unable to provide signature?

definitions.meaning: split as ..., zero pens, so there is nothing to sign with

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: read the answer as the letter O (nothing) and PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open is candid and plain-spoken, just as a frank person is.

clue.text: Records perhaps concerned with contracts

parts.note: re means about, concerning
leases are rental contracts

explanation.surface: Documents dealing with agreements, it seems, are being filed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Records' looks like documents, but means records issued by a music label.
explanation.definitionFit: New records, films or singles put out to the public are issues, also called new releases.

clue.text: Strong fastening

definitions.meaning: binding with a band or belt

explanation.definitionFit: The word means sturdy and well built, and also securing something with belts.

clue.text: Go-getter getting back out of dreary country in recession

indicators.note: out of means the letters for back are removed from the word dreary

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: in recession means the country is read backwards, receding

parts.note: Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: An ambitious type gets back on his feet after leaving a dull country whose economy is shrinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing REAR from DREARY leaves DY; NAMO is OMAN backwards. 'Getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is an energetic, forceful person, a go-getter in figurative use.

clue.text: Broken nose requires completely new bandaging, a state

indicators.note: bandaging means wrapping round, so the word for new surrounds the jumbled nose

parts.note: in mint condition means completely new

indicators.note: broken signals the letters of nose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken nose needs a fresh dressing in some condition or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' scrambles nose and 'bandaging' wraps the word for brand new round it; 'requires' is only a link, and 'state' looks like condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is a US state in the Upper Midwest.

clue.text: At the outset, telephone number secure

indicators.note: at the outset picks the opening letter of telephone

parts.note: number here is something that numbs, and ether is an anaesthetic

explanation.surface: First, the phone number must be made safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but a thing that makes numb: ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: To tether an animal or boat is to tie it up, making it fast and secure.

clue.text: What beef is to Hindu, I say

definitions.meaning: cattle are sacred in Hinduism, so beef comes from a sacred animal

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild expletive of surprise, and literally a sacred animal to Hindus.

clue.text: Superior instrument that's moved right to the front in craft

indicators.note: in places the shifted instrument inside the word for craft

parts.note: craft means skill, art

indicators.note: moved shows a letter of the instrument shifting position within it
to the front says where the shifted letter for right ends up: at the start

parts.note: an organ is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A haughty musician's instrument is rearranged within a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat but means skill; 'that's moved right to the front' shifts the R of the instrument to its start, and 'in' places the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior in the sense of supercilious or condescending is close to haughty and arrogant.

clue.text: Face, horrid one

parts.note: grim means horrid, forbidding
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A horrid one's countenance.
explanation.definitionFit: To grimace is to make a contorted face, here used as a noun for such an expression.

clue.text: Test spirit of optimism when case dismissed

indicators.note: the case is the outside of a word, so its first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: morale is the confident spirit of a group

explanation.surface: A trial ends happily for a defendant as the case against them is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case dismissed' looks legal; it removes the outer letters of MORALE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, a test conducted by speech.

clue.text: Wine and one soft drink in Ronda, lacking body

indicators.note: in places the numeral and drink inside the shell of the town
lacking body leaves only the outside letters of the town Ronda

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
OJ is orange juice

explanation.surface: In the Spanish town of Ronda, a tourist orders wine and a juice, wanting something light.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronda is a town in Andalusia, fitting the Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red Spanish wine from the La Rioja region.

clue.text: Big-hitter, banker after a lot of money heading for disaster

indicators.note: after places the banker following the earlier pieces

parts.note: a pile is a fortune, a lot of money

indicators.note: heading for picks the first letter of disaster

parts.note: a banker is crossword slang for a river, something that has banks

explanation.surface: A financier chasing a fortune is on course for ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is not a financier but a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A piledriver is a machine that hammers posts into the ground, so a figurative big hitter.

clue.text: As before dark, in twilit thicket observation starts

indicators.note: starts picks the first letter of each of the five words that come before it

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's evening session, peering into a shady copse at dusk as before.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to say the same again, repeating what was said earlier.

clue.text: Dishonest, unlike Pinocchio's conscience?

definitions.meaning: in the Disney film Pinocchio's conscience is Jiminy Cricket, so anything else is literally something other than a cricket

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is the British game of fair play, so the phrase means unfair; Pinocchio's conscience is the insect Jiminy Cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling conduct unsporting this way, after the game's fair-play ideal, means it is unfair or underhand.

clue.text: Have on a type of leather

definitions.meaning: soft leather made from young goat skin

explanation.definitionFit: To kid is to tease or fool; kid is also soft goatskin leather used for gloves.

clue.text: Old German forgoing introduction: some nerve!

indicators.note: forgoing its introduction means the first letter is dropped from the people

parts.note: the Saxons were an ancient Germanic people

explanation.surface: An ancient warrior strides in unannounced, which takes some cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some nerve!' looks like an exclamation at cheek; it means part of a nerve cell.
explanation.definitionFit: An axon is the long fibre of a nerve cell, so part of the nervous tissue.

clue.text: Stud's home? Scold the crawler

parts.note: a stud earring sits in the ear
to wig someone is an old verb for to scold or rebuke

explanation.surface: A horse breeder at a stud farm tells off some creeping toady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stud' suggests horses but is an earring.
explanation.definitionFit: An earwig is a small insect that creeps along the ground, a crawling bug.

clue.text: See description in code as cryptic

indicators.note: cryptic means mysterious or puzzling, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter's instruction to look at a clue described in a secret cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a bishop's see, not look.
explanation.definitionFit: Diocesan is the adjective for a bishop's diocese, so it describes a see.
